## Learning goals

- I can transfer dimensions from an approved drawing to the material.
- I can explain what each possible project tool is used for.
- I can follow the approved build sequence and document the finished holder.
- I can test the holder against the design requirements and record an improvement.

## Tools and what they do

The available tools and the approved process will vary by shop.

- **Ruler:** measures distances and transfers dimensions from the drawing to the material.
- **Square:** lays out straight lines at 90 degrees and helps relate one feature to a reference edge.
- **Pencil:** records cut lines, hole centres, reference lines, labels, and other layout information.
- **Hand saw:** cuts stock manually and may be used for straightforward rough or finished cuts.
- **Scroll saw:** uses a narrow moving blade to cut curves, outside profiles, and some openings or notches.
- **Band saw:** uses a continuous blade to cut stock, straight lines, and outside curves.
- **Drill press:** uses a rotating bit held in a fixed machine to make positioned holes.
- **Coping saw:** uses a narrow hand-operated blade for curves, notches, and small adjustments.
- **Edge sander:** uses a moving abrasive surface to refine suitable straight or outside edges.
- **Drum sander:** uses a cylindrical abrasive to refine curved edges or openings.
- **Orbital sander:** uses a small orbital motion to finish broad, accessible surfaces.
- **Oscillating sander:** moves an abrasive spindle or belt while it sands and is often used for shaped edges and inside curves.
- **Sanding by hand:** refines details, breaks sharp edges, smooths surfaces, and adjusts fit where a machine is not appropriate.

## Build sequence

### 1. Confirm the approved design

Use the drawing approved by the instructor. Construction students may follow the [premade dimensions and order of operations](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1rdGC6nsCR6Z5DtoN071NhLQZxIc3XbFz0cQT_RCSFDs/edit?gid=452419533#gid=452419533). Students making an original holder should complete the [Phone Holder Design](../cad-parametric-modeling/phone-holder-design.qmd) first.

### 2. Measure and lay out the parts

Transfer the outside edges, hole centres, slots, and notches from the approved drawing. Use consistent reference edges, label the parts, and check the layout against the drawing.

### 3. Cut the stock and outside shapes

The approved process may use a hand saw, scroll saw, or band saw for the stock and outside profiles.

### 4. Drill the opening

The approved process may use the drill press for the required opening.

### 5. Cut the notches

The approved process may use a coping saw or scroll saw for the notches that connect the parts.

### 6. Refine the edges

The approved process may use the edge sander for suitable straight or outside edges and a drum or oscillating sander for suitable curved edges or openings.

### 7. Finish sanding

Finish the surfaces with an orbital sander, oscillating sander, drum sander, or sanding by hand, as specified in the approved process.

### 8. Fit, test, and improve

Assemble the parts and test the holder with the intended device. Check stability, part fit, access to the screen and controls, charging-cable clearance, surface finish, and any added function from the design brief. Record one improvement made after testing.

## Check your work

- [ ] The layout matches the approved drawing.
- [ ] The parts fit without being forced.
- [ ] The holder is stable with the intended device.
- [ ] The surfaces and edges meet the required finish.
- [ ] Any added function works as intended.
- [ ] The finished build and improvement are documented.

## Save and submit

Follow the [digital drawing submission](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1NgAOEpUvRkkanlb8MvY5porLpp18FNvFNbXxHZ6il-4/edit?tab=t.0). Include the Onshape link, an isometric screenshot, and a photo of the finished phone holder.

Use clear filenames that begin with your student number and last name, such as `123456789-Smith-phone-holder-isometric.png`.

## Common issues

- **The notches are loose:** compare the finished notch with the drawing and the actual material thickness.
- **The holder tips:** compare the result with the intended phone position, base contact, shelf depth, and back angle.
- **The phone covers a feature:** test the actual device against the approved design.
- **Sanding changed the fit:** compare the mating surfaces with the dimensions and the other parts.
- **An added feature is not useful:** return to the situation, opportunity, and user needs.
